text:
Aisha Patel: quick heads-up — monitoring alerted on persistent Xid/ ECC spikes from a subset of nodes in ded-gpu-pool-eu1 this morning. I want a short customer comm we can send to Dedicated & Private customers on affected hosts. draft below and ops notes after.

ops-bot: ALERT: GPU ECC correction rate > threshold on nodes: eu1-node-47, eu1-node-48. 42 Xid errors in last 3h. Auto-drain triggered on eu1-node-48.

Priya Rao: thanks — we already started a controlled drain on eu1-node-48 at 08:12 UTC. Traffic shifted to warm spares, so no immediate customer impact observed, but error counts on 47 look wobblier.

Marcos Li: hardware note: ECC corrections that convert to Xid often mean early memory degradation. We can replace GPUs but need to book cross-region spare for eu1 — ETA 36-60h depending on courier. If 47 trends, we'll plan hot-swap, but prefer to validate board-level telemetry first.

Evan Brooks: customer comm draft (short, non-technical) — please comment: 
``` 
Hi — we're contacting you about scheduled maintenance for GPU capacity in eu-west (Dedicated/Private). Earlier today, we detected elevated memory-correction and machine errors on a small number of nodes that serve Dedicated capacity. To avoid any risk to your workloads we have drained one node and will replace the affected GPU hardware. Your capacity has been routed to redundant capacity and we do not expect service interruption.

Planned next steps:
- Immediate: continued routing away from affected nodes (already in effect).
- 0-72h: hardware replacement and validation; we'll run thorough tests before returning nodes to rotation.
- Impact: no planned downtime; we will post updates if timelines change.

If you have strict locality requirements or capacity reservations that might be affected, please reply and we'll coordinate a maintenance window.

Regards,
Redwood Inference Support
```

Priya Rao: edit suggestion: add a short note about data residency and whether failover kept pinned VPC tenancy — e.g., "Failover preserves your VPC and tenancy; traffic was routed to spare hardware in the same region." keeps customers reassured.

Marcos Li: ops detail for CS (internal): replacement workflow — 1) confirm ECC/Xid historical trend via nvml logs, 2) drain and failover (done on 48), 3) schedule physical swap (ETA 36-60h), 4) post-swap burn-in (2-4h) + telemetry check, 5) return to pool behind canary traffic for 1h. If replacement delayed, we may keep nodes drained longer.

Aisha Patel: good. Evan can you add the residency sentence and a short timeline bullet with ETA window? Then we'll send as an "affected host" notice to customers with pinned Dedicated capacity in eu-west. Also include a brief internal ops note to be sent as an attachment if customers ask for more technical detail.

Evan Brooks: updated draft: 
``` 
Hi — we wanted to notify you about a proactive maintenance action in eu-west affecting a small subset of Dedicated/Private hosts. Earlier today we detected elevated memory-correction and machine errors on two nodes. To protect your workloads we drained one node and rerouted traffic to redundant capacity in-region. We will replace the affected GPU hardware and validate the nodes before returning them to service.

Planned next steps and ETA:
- Immediate: traffic routed away from affected hosts (in-region).
- 0–72 hours: hardware replacement, burn-in, and validation. We expect replacement to complete within 36–60 hours; burn-in and validation may extend this to the 72h window.
- Impact: no planned downtime. If you have strict locality or reserved-capacity constraints, reply and we will coordinate an explicit maintenance window.

Failover and data residency: failover preserves your VPC, tenancy, and in-region placement; we did not move workloads out of eu-west.

If you'd like the technical ops summary (nvml logs, Xid counts, replacement ticket), reply and we can share.

Regards,
Redwood Inference Support
```

Priya Rao: LGTM. Marcos, confirm ETA so we don't overpromise.

Marcos Li: confirmed: parts on order, courier ETA 36–60h. I'll update if we can do next-day.

Aisha Patel: OK let's send this to impacted customers in the next 30m. Evan — drop the internal ops summary as an attachment to the ticket thread and set expectation to share logs only on request. I'll post a short internal note in eng-runtime and eng-sre channels.

ops-bot: ticket created: HW-12487 (eu1 node replacement). Assigned to Marcos Li.

Evan Brooks: sending now. I'll post the message and paste thread IDs here when done.

Aisha Patel: thanks everyone. keep this thread for updates.
